Subject: Pricing + Latency trade-offs — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for taking time today, Samir — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps on pricing and latency trade-offs based on the volumes you shared.

TL;DR: For your expected 1.5-3B tokens/month profile, we recommend evaluating the Dedicated Standard tier with burst capacity for peak windows, and a mixed strategy of streamed low-latency routes for user-facing flows (SLO 100-200ms) and batched generation for async/pipeline jobs to reduce unit costs. See attached pricing tiers and an estimate CSV.

Summary of what you told us on the call:
- Monthly token run rate (current/prospective): ~1.5B steady, spikes to ~3B during month-end reporting windows
- Latency SLOs: interactive widgets need sub-200ms; daily batch scoring can accept >2s
- Target budget: headed for a $/1M-token budget conversation — stated target range $500-$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on latency

Preliminary unit economics guidance (high level):
- Hosted API, realtime (streaming) low-latency path: ~ $1,400 - $2,200 per 1M tokens at 100-200ms SLOs (depends on model variant and concurrency)
- Hosted API, relaxed latency / batched path: ~ $600 - $1,000 per 1M tokens (2s+ SLO, heavy batching)
- Dedicated (committed): ~ $350 - $850 per 1M tokens depending on commitment level, quantization, and effective batching/caching gains

Actions / next steps:
1) I attached a draft pricing tiers doc and a CSV with the run-rate estimates. Please confirm token mix: what fraction is interactive vs batch? (We used 40/60 interactive/batch in the estimate.)
2) If you can share a sample 24-hr traffic trace or a few representative request types (avg tokens in/out, percent streamed) we’ll produce a more precise cost model and an SLO-aware recommendation.
3) If the target is to hit ~$1,000/1M tokens across all workloads, we’ll likely propose Dedicated with an autoscale burst pool + streaming for the critical path.

Happy to hop on a short follow-up tomorrow to walk the numbers.

Great questions — answered inline below. I'll also attach a one-pager example hitting a $1,000/1M token target.

Q1 — concrete example for $1,000/1M:
- Example config: Dedicated Standard (4xA100-equivalent pool), moderate commit (12 months), mixed workload. Assumptions: 60% batched scoring (2s+ SLO) with efficient batching, 40% interactive streaming. We assume model quantized to 8-bit where compatible and prefix caching reduces repeated context tokens by ~15%.
- Resulting blended price: ~ $980 - $1,050 per 1M tokens (depending on hit-rate of the cache and actual batch sizes).
- Key levers: increase batching for non-interactive jobs, enable KV/prefix caching, and move less-sensitive paths to cheaper model variants.

Q2 — streaming vs batching for sub-200ms:
- Streaming is the most reliable way to hit <200ms tail latency for varied request sizes, especially with unpredictable concurrency.
- You can use micro-batching and aggressive autoscale to approximate interactive latency, but that typically raises cost and requires more complex tuning. So: streaming for user-facing UI; batching for background jobs.

Q3 — Dedicated commitments to hit $350-$850 band:
- $350/1M is the low end and requires: large annual commitment (multi-million token equivalent), high utilization (>75%), and use of quantized models + reserved capacity with autoscale headroom.
- $600-$850 is reachable with mid-sized 12-month commit and reasonable utilization (40–70%), plus some batching and cache optimizations.

I’ve attached the example one-pager (redwood_pricing_tiers_v2.pdf) plus the estimated_token_run_rates.csv. If you confirm your interactive/batch split and share simple traffic samples we’ll run a deterministic model and deliver a slide with the recommended Dedicated configuration and expected blended $/1M number.

Would you and procurement prefer we present the numbers live on Wed or send the deterministic model beforehand?

Best,
Marissa

Hi Samir — quick note from the platform/sre side: if your team has strict SLOs (esp. 99th percentile targets), we typically recommend an SLO-driven pricing conversation:

- We define routes by latency SLO (e.g., interactive <200ms; low-latency batch <500ms; high-throughput batch >2s).
- Each route can map to a different pricing metric / unit price (streamed tokens vs batched tokens) because cost to serve differs materially.
- For predictable pricing, Dedicated + slot reservations for interactive pools with pre-warmed KV caches is the cheapest way to meet tight tail SLOs.

Operational knobs to optimize cost without jeopardizing SLOs:
- Continuous batching for batch routes (auto-batch sizes aligned to latency window)
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context across calls (saves tokens and compute)
- Streaming only on the interactive route; use chunked streaming for larger responses to reduce tail variance
- Model fallbacks: run a cheaper variant for tails or non-critical requests with automatic fallback when the primary is saturated

If you want, Dev and I can run a quick config sweep against your sample trace and produce a table: expected cost per 1M tokens under three SLO mixes.
